thread:
Sasha: Anyone seeing token/sec drop on the continuous-batcher after last night's release? canary shows queue depth rising fast and tokensec down ~30%
Mike: Yup, spotted it in canary and a single dedicated shard. tail latency up too. looks like underfilled batches stacking.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout paused for release/ctb-2026-03-15 at 3425006789 :no_entry_sign:
Anya: I profiled one of the canary pods, saw a bunch of memcpy spikes during kernel selection. grabbing perf output now:
Anya: ```
# perf top sample
0.  35.4%  runtime  [kernel]  memcpy
1.  12.1%  runtime  runtime::kernel_selector::choose
2.   8.7%  runtime  scheduler::coalesce::drain
```
Reena: That stack suggests kernel selector falling back to a memcopy-heavy path (cuda memcpy + pack) for many batches, esp mixed-seq lengths. Did something change in prefetch/padding heuristics?
Mike: There's a scheduler_prefetch tweak in PR #472 that reduced padding and shuffled affinity thresholds. Could be toggling kernel policy for short seqs.
Sasha: Can we bisect the change range quickly? @Mike - can you run the perf bisect script across the week of merges?
Mike: Starting bisect now. Running: ./tools/bisect_perf --metric tokensec --range 2026-03-10..2026-03-15 --cluster canary
deploy-bot: CI perf check: integration-run-885 (2026-03-15 merge) flagged tokensec -28% vs baseline.
Anya: I reproduced locally with seed 42. Repro steps: 
Anya: ```
./run_perf --batcher continuous --seqdist mixed --seed 42 --profile
# observe kernel=memcopy path when batch_estimate < 4
```
Reena: Logs show kernel_selector::score produced lower local_affinity after the scheduler change. It then picks the fallback that does an extra pack+memcpy.
Sasha: Two immediate remediations: force kernel affinity back to previous threshold OR revert the prefetch change. Which is safer for production?
Mike: Safer is revert PR #472 (commit abc1234). I'll prepare the revert PR and test canary.
Mike: Revert PR opened: #478 (revert of #472). merging to canary now.
deploy-bot: Revert merged to canary branch, rollout scheduled. Observability will post metrics in ~10m.
Sasha: Thanks, Mike. If canary looks green we can unpause rollout.
ops-bot: Canary metrics update: tokensec recovered to 97-102% of baseline within 7m post-revert. queue depth normalized. :white_check_mark:
Sasha: Excellent — marking this as rollout blocker resolved. We'll follow up with a safer throttled change to prefetch padding and add a perf unit test around kernel choice.
Reena: I'll add a regression test that asserts kernel_selector doesn't flip to memcopy path for mixed-seq workloads under typical batch sizes.
Mike: Filed follow-up: #479 - add kernel selection perf regression test + telemetry for memcopy path ratio.
Sasha: Nice. Closing loop here. :thumbsup:
